nodes.label: The Forwarding Loop
nodes.rationale: The orchestrator's whole control structure: next, act, report, repeat until done. The split exists so all between-stage routing (scope resolution, flag precedence, jump direction, resume/init guards, sequencing, gate status, completion) is owned deterministically by the tool and never re-derived in prose, leaving the conductor only the quality of execution inside the named move. next is read-only and mutates nothing; report commits the transition so the next next reads fresh state. A malformed directive is reported plainly and stops the loop rather than being improvised around.

nodes.label: Typed Directive
nodes.rationale: Exactly one JSON directive per next call, whose kind names the single move to make. Eight kinds are emitted today (load-steering, run-stage, invoke-swarm, ask, print, error, done, parked); dispatch-subagent and present-gate remain documented placeholders so the loop is complete-shaped, and implementing them speculatively is forbidden.

nodes.label: run-stage Directive
nodes.rationale: Carries stage_file, consumes, memory_path, rules_in_context, inline_context_paths, mode, gate, unit and single. Context loading is scoped by topology on purpose: lead plus supports on inline, lead only on mob, none on fully dispatched subagent/pipeline - and agent names alone are never loaded context. The branch order is single first, then gate.

nodes.label: load-steering Directive
nodes.rationale: Transport, not stage work: rules_content is applied in array order and retained as the active bundle, then continue is called with the continue_token, repeating until run-stage. It is never reported, and loading rules is deliberately unspoken because it is not an event in the user's project.

nodes.label: invoke-swarm Directive
nodes.rationale: Emitted only for an eligible Construction batch under an autonomous grant, and orthogonal to the reserved agent-team stage mode. The live session is the conductor and owns fan-out and retry; aidlc-swarm.ts is a deterministic referee that is consulted, never a loop-owner - prepare forks an isolated worktree per unit so parallel units cannot collide.

nodes.label: ask Directive
nodes.rationale: The engine never calls AskUserQuestion itself - it defers the human turn to the conductor, who renders directive.question and feeds the verbatim answer back on the next report via --user-input. Any resume-menu answer reports result resumed and then acts on the returned per-choice print.

nodes.label: gate unresolved Sentinel
nodes.rationale: The single non-deterministic gate case, handed back to the conductor because no parser can derive a team's walking-skeleton stance from free-form practices prose. The stage body must not run until the stance is classified and returned to the engine - a deliberate carve-out in an otherwise tool-owned routing surface.

nodes.label: Walking-Skeleton Stance Classification
nodes.rationale: Resolved by reading the '## Walking Skeleton' section across org, team then project memory with the most-specific non-empty statement winning: always/every greenfield feature maps to on, never maps to off, scope-dependent or unspecified defers to the scope's own skeleton declaration.

nodes.label: PRE-GENERATION SUMMARY STOP
nodes.rationale: A mandatory human checkpoint after any file-backed Q&A and before any artifact exists: append the Consolidated Summary Confirmation section, record the prompt with a checkpoint-specific decision receipt, render the unlettered Looks correct / Request changes choice, and treat Q&A as incomplete until the file holds the human's exact answer and the receipt command succeeds. It is not bypassed even on the isolated single-stage path, and it never merges with the reviewer, learnings or approval steps.

nodes.label: Reviewer Contract
nodes.rationale: The reviewer receives the stage definition, Q&A file and artifact paths - plus resolved consumes on per-unit stages so cross-unit contract claims can be checked against shared inception artifacts - but deliberately never memory.md or plan.md. Every invocation is bracketed by REVIEW_REQUESTED and REVIEW_COMPLETED receipts, a lost verdict is recovered with --retry-pending against the same unmatched request without consuming an iteration, and in the autonomous swarm a unit is not claimable at finalize merely because check passed.

nodes.label: Learnings Ritual
nodes.rationale: surface, then a structured question plus free-text channel, then an admission conflict-check against org.md, then persist. The 'Anything to add?' question must carry at least two explicit options and is asked even when surface returns zero candidates, because inferring 'Nothing to add' would let the loop silently skip the only sanctioned path for turning a human correction into a persistent practice in team.md or project.md.

nodes.label: Per-Unit Iteration
nodes.rationale: When directive.unit is present the run-stage is one iteration of a for_each unit-of-work Construction stage (the 3.1-3.4 design stages plus code-generation): question flow, summary stop and reviewer all run for THIS unit with --unit threaded through the log commands, artifacts land under construction/<unit>/<stage>/, and the engine - not the conductor - drives the loop.

nodes.label: Conductor Persona Delivery
nodes.rationale: The irreducible execution-quality charter is authored once and baked by the engine into the first run-stage directive's conductor_persona field rather than loaded from a path, so every entry point receives the same charter and no caller can load a stale or partial copy by hand.

nodes.label: narration Field
nodes.rationale: Worded by the tool that knows the facts: when present it is what the user hears about the step, reproduced with only tense/name corrections and never accompanied by a further account of the mechanism; when absent the step is carried out silently. Speech is carried by exactly two things - a narration value between steps and a SAY line's quoted text inside a step - with one exception, the very first turn, where no next has returned yet and a single sentence about the user's own request is allowed.

nodes.label: Quiet-In-Between Voice Rule
nodes.rationale: An expert working alongside someone does not narrate keystrokes, so the resting state between tool calls is no prose at all. The rule bites on paraphrase as well as jargon: a friendlier phrasing of internal routing is still that sentence. The working test - when a sentence's only content is which step comes next, make the tool call instead - and the Construction carve-out (iteration passes, continuation tokens, produces lists all stay internal) both follow from it.

nodes.label: Adaptive Workflow Composer
nodes.rationale: Dispatched as an agent that runs a read-only detect scan and estimates five entropy components, then proposes an EXECUTE/SKIP grid presented as three blocks behind an approve/edit/reject gate. Presentation leads with a plain-language recommendation rather than scores, and counts come from the validator, never a hand recount. Division of labour: the composer proposes, the human decides, the deterministic validator guards, and the conductor never improvises a grid in prose. A custom grid needs BOTH the scope .md and the scope-grid.json entry, since a .md without a grid entry resolves as all-SKIP. In-flight recompose uses a pending marker written before the gate and deleted the moment it resolves, flips only pending ahead-of-cursor stages, and audits RECOMPOSED instead of hand-editing state.

nodes.label: Scope-to-Stage Mapping
nodes.rationale: Source of truth is one file per scope under .claude/scopes/ (identity, keywords, description, skeleton default) plus each stage's scopes: frontmatter for membership, transposed into the compiled grid by aidlc-graph.ts compile. The in-skill table is regenerated human-readable data, explicitly not dispatch logic and never hand-edited; the one sanctioned write path is the composer appending an approved composed scope.

nodes.label: Compiled Stage Graph
nodes.rationale: 32 stages across initialization, ideation, inception, construction and operation, each with phase, ALWAYS/CONDITIONAL execution, lead and support agents and a run mode. The engine reads data/stage-graph.json directly for all routing; the table in the skill is the generated mirror. Only four stages are non-inline: reverse-engineering (pipeline), practices-discovery (subagent), user-stories (mob) and code-generation (subagent).

nodes.label: Single-Stage Isolation
nodes.rationale: An isolated run keeps the full ritual (summary stop, artifacts, diary, reviewer, verification) but commits under a synthetic workflow id and never advances Current Stage - the tool refuses to. --single is threaded through the checkpoint decision/answer pair and both reviewer log calls precisely so those receipts cannot be mistaken for satisfying the main workflow.

nodes.label: Stage Ritual Atomicity
nodes.rationale: Once a stage starts every step fires - questions, artifact, reviewer, learnings, gate - and none is skippable. 'Skip to stage X' skips intermediate stages, never the target's own ritual, and the current stage including learnings must complete before jumping.

nodes.label: Autonomy Is Never Inferred
nodes.rationale: 'Go with recommended' is a one-time instruction for that stage only; the next stage starts fresh, autonomy is never carried forward, and questions are never self-answered without explicit permission for the specific stage.

nodes.label: Second-Intent Offer
nodes.rationale: Classifying each new input as continuation, genuinely new work, or plan-reshape is knowledge-work reserved to the conductor because the read-only engine never births alongside a live intent. Default to continuation; on genuine new work offer rather than auto-birth, naming the inferred scope so the human can correct it and leading the affirmative option with 'Yes', since starting a workflow is a mutation gated on a human yes. A reshape request must route through the compose verb, because a freeform mid-flow next would silently advance the current stage instead.

nodes.label: Parking a Workflow
nodes.rationale: An enterprise-scope run need not finish in one session: park stops cleanly at the current inter-stage boundary, advancing nothing and marking nothing complete, and exists so a low-context conductor never fabricates approvals to reach done. Resume is /aidlc --resume, which clears the park marker.

nodes.label: Audit Event Naming Discipline
nodes.rationale: Event types come only from the shared audit-format reference and are never invented. State transitions are tool-owned: the engine's report step and the stage tools own every emission, and no audit event is ever written from prose - so each lifecycle outcome is reported exactly once and a speculative direct lifecycle call hits the state guard.

nodes.label: Mandatory Protocol Loading
nodes.rationale: Three protocols load at fixed moments rather than on judgement: the stage protocol on every stage, the recovery protocol on session resume or a mid-stage change event, and the governance protocol at phase boundaries to run the phase-boundary traceability verification.

hyperedges.label: Ordered stage-completion sequence: summary stop, reviewer, learnings, gate
